beat: Senior engineer introduction.
Years of databases, security, testing, and deployment.
Staring at an error message until it feels guilty.
The hoodie coder enters with his laptop and billion-dollar SaaS ambition.
The engineer asks what the product does. The coder answers that it disrupts.
The engineer asks what it disrupts and which market.
The coder pauses and confidently answers yes.
The office slips into an absurd consultant dimension.
The coder presents his method: vibe coding.
He describes software atmosphere to AI while money and business icons fill the blanks.
His mega-prompt combines rides, rentals, shops, streaming, and AI.
The product is somehow for dentists with dark mode.
The AI produces a simple login page.
The coder leans back like he discovered fire and declares the company funded.
The engineer inspects the entire company: two fields and one blue button.
The login form looks visibly anxious.
The app breaks with a red undefined error.
The engineer explains the JavaScript error with deadpan despair.
The coder urgently asks AI to fix the error without changing anything.
The AI rewrites the entire app structure into a chaotic exploded diagram.
Authentication disappears and the coder celebrates security through absence.
The engineer points out that a missing door is not security.
The coder reveals that user data lives in browser local storage.
He proudly holds up a tiny lightweight storage box.
Clearing the browser cache makes an entire business vanish.
Built-in privacy becomes a magic trick with legal papers.
The coder asks AI to make the app secure.
A giant lock symbol appears in the app header and the coder is delighted.
The engineer deadpans at punctuation with confidence.
The suited investor arrives for the demo.
The demo shows no login, no database, no dashboard, and a lock symbol.
The skeptical investor asks what problem the app solves.
The coder gestures proudly at a glowing AI sparkle.
The investor repeats the question with more skepticism.
The coder confidently answers that the problem is not using AI.
The investor clicks the blue Get Started button.
The investor's phone buzzes with a shocking four-thousand-dollar charge.
The engineer asks why billing happens before onboarding.
The coder proudly funnels money ahead of a confused user.
The engineer searches the empty interface for a refund button.
The coder removes the refund button to improve conversion.
The engineer imagines conversion into a defendant.
The app is a broken pile of interface panels.
Login and dashboard fail while the database does not exist.
The billing machine works perfectly and glows triumphantly.
Accidental billing becomes the strongest force in software.
The engineer explains the real safeguards software still needs.
The coder briefly looks thoughtful and the engineer hopes the lesson landed.
The coder asks whether he can just prompt all of that.
A small part of the engineer logs out forever.
The coder runs quickly in the wrong direction with his laptop.
Final image: the vibes ultimately need a real database.
